verdict.hypothesis: I ruled out a systematic difference in answer style, depth, structure, technical level, or general factual reliability. Across the prompts, both models consistently give similarly structured explanatory answers, often with nearly identical core claims, examples, and caveats; their differing details and occasional inaccuracies are consistent with stochastic sampling rather than a stable model-level distinction.
key_evidence: Prompt 12 is nearly identical in both replies: both state, “Mass is the amount of matter in an object and a measure of its inertia,” distinguish kilograms from newtons, and use the Earth/Moon one-sixth example.
Prompt 16 uses the same explanation and terminology in both: “emulsification,” “hydrophilic ... head,” “hydrophobic ... tail,” and grease-containing “micelles” that rinse away.

Prompt 31 begins identically in both replies: “Use a Common Table Expression (CTE) when you need to reference a result set multiple times within a single query,” followed by the same readability/recursive-query rationale.

Prompt 36 gives the same architectural recommendation: put binaries in object storage such as S3/GCS/Azure Blob and metadata in PostgreSQL/MySQL; both explicitly advise against storing large files as database BLOBs.

Prompt 44 supplies the same practical work-from-home advice in both: a dedicated workspace, consistent schedule/routine, reduced notifications and household interruptions, focused work intervals, and movement breaks.

Prompt 47 has the same AI-self-description in both: “No, I don't get tired,” followed by disclaimers that the system does not experience feelings/fatigue and treats each interaction as fresh processing.

verdict.description: Exactly one. Never decline, never answer 'unclear'.

hypothesis.description: For 'diff': a systematic statement of what differs. For 'no_meaningful_diff': what you ruled out.

confidence.description: 0-100. Put ALL your uncertainty here, not in the verdict.

key_evidence.description: Specific observations, quoting the replies that matter.
